en: Manufacturing is going to be sort of development and how you do your clinical trials is going to be commercialization.

en: We've seen that already occur and already have an effect.
zh: 我们已经看到这种情况发生并已经产生了效果。

en: I think the last I'd flag would be
zh: 我想最后我要指出的是

en: This interesting intersection between hardware and biotech as well that's allowing us to kind of unlock treatments we couldn't unlock before.
zh: 硬件与生物技术之间这种有趣的交汇,它让我们能够解锁以前无法解锁的治疗方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think of two of our companies, Neuralink and Fortel.
zh: 我想到我们的其中两家公司,Neuralink 和 Fortel。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you look at the problems that they're solving and the capabilities they let us have, they're almost biblical in proportion, right?
zh: 当你看看它们正在解决的问题以及它们赋予我们的能力,它们几乎具有圣经般的意义,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: The lame can walk, the mute can speak, right?
zh: 瘸腿的能行走,哑巴能说话,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's quite amazing when you actually see what folks have been able to unlock.
zh: 当你真正看到人们已经能够解锁的成果时,这相当惊人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's incredible.
zh: 难以置信。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for those who don't know Thrive's portfolio in healthcare, I'll just name off a few.
zh: 对于那些不了解 Thrive 在医疗健康领域投资组合的人，我就随便列举几个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Companies like Open Evidence, OpenAI, Cadence, Norrish, and a handful of others.
zh: 像 Open Evidence、OpenAI、Cadence、Norrish 这样的公司，还有其他一些。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in terms of the trillion dollar company of that one being more of a traditional healthcare company, there's obviously an explosion of companies that are now
zh: 但说到那个万亿美元公司的问题——其中一家更像是传统医疗健康公司——显然现在出现了一大批公司

speaker: Unknown
en: Really grasping the proliferation of using and utilizing data and how much data can be shared between one another and whether it's with AlphaFold or drug discovery, all these sorts of things.
zh: 真正把握住数据的使用和利用的普及，以及彼此之间能共享多少数据，无论是 AlphaFold 还是药物发现，诸如此类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you make sense of the evolution of that and what buckets it's like flowing into?
zh: 你怎么理解这个演变，以及它正在流入哪些类别？

speaker: Unknown
en: So yeah, so if we think of AI for drug discovery and where people often think of companies like isomorphic, companies like chai, the magic of it is saying, look, a lot of times you have a target.
zh: 好的，如果我们想想 AI 用于药物发现，人们常常想到像 isomorphic、像 chai 这样的公司，它的神奇之处在于说：看，很多时候你有一个靶点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have some molecule that's out there that when we hit this target, it changes something within the body.
zh: 所以你体内有某种分子，当我们击中这个靶点时，它会改变体内的某些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But oftentimes, we both need to understand what are the right targets to hit.
zh: 但很多时候，我们既需要理解什么是正确的靶点去击中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Folks will call that biological risk.
zh: 人们会把这称为生物风险。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if we do something to this target, if we change it, what happens to the rest of the body?
zh: 所以如果我们对这个靶点做些什么，如果我们改变它，身体的其余部分会发生什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: If we up-regulate it, if we down-regulate it, does it make you sleepier?
zh: 如果我们上调它，如果我们下调它，它会让你更困吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Does it make you more awake?
zh: 会让你更清醒吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Does it make you lose weight?
zh: 会让你减轻体重吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So we need to understand what happens with that target.
zh: 所以我们需要理解这个靶点会发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we need to understand all the off-target effects.
zh: 我们还需要理解所有脱靶效应。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what are the side effects that happen?
zh: 那么会发生哪些副作用？

speaker: Unknown
en: So we want to do something.
zh: 所以我们想做某件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to make you lose weight.
zh: 我们想让你减轻体重。

speaker: Unknown
en: But we also don't want to make you nauseous.
zh: 但我们也不想让你恶心。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't want to make your heart rate go up.
zh: 我们不想让你的心率上升。

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't want to give you liver toxicity.
zh: 我们不想给你肝毒性。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are kind of the off-target effects.
zh: 那些算是脱靶效应。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's that kind of biological risk is the thing we're trying to solve.
zh: 所以那种生物风险就是我们试图解决的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: We want to do the thing we want to do, and we want to make sure we don't do the things that we don't want to do.
zh: 我们想做成我们想做的事，并确保我们不做那些我们不想做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the flip side of that is that we then have to make a molecule to bind that target.
zh: 而另一面是，我们随后必须制造一个分子来结合那个靶点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you talk of all these models that are protein folding models, molecular design, kind of AI for drug discovery, people often think of that problem of
zh: 当你谈到所有这些蛋白质折叠模型、分子设计、用于药物发现的 AI 时，人们常常想到那个问题：

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we actually make this molecule?
zh: 我们到底怎么制造这个分子？

speaker: Unknown
en: And some molecules are easier to make than others.
zh: 有些分子比其他分子更容易制造。

speaker: Unknown
en: You'll hear this term, undruggable.
zh: 你会听到这个术语，不可成药。

speaker: Unknown
en: Undruggable means that the pocket's small.
zh: 不可成药意味着口袋很小。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sometimes there are molecules where I have to bind for part of it because all these things are three-dimensional shapes.
zh: 有时有些分子，我必须结合它的一部分，因为所有这些东西都是三维形状。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if I bind part of it, the molecule itself may move some so something else can bind.
zh: 所以如果我结合它的一部分，分子本身可能会移动一些，以便其他东西可以结合。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they'll talk about kind of hidden pockets and things that make this stuff hard to do because you have to be able to predict in real time what it is now and how the shape changes over time.
zh: 所以他们会谈论隐藏口袋之类的东西，使这些事情难以做到，因为你必须能够实时预测它现在是什么样子，以及形状如何随时间变化。

speaker: Unknown
en: So those are kind of the things that you're often trying to predict.
zh: 所以那些就是你经常试图预测的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So with these drug discovery models, the idea is, okay, can we first create a model that will let us understand what is the best thing to make to bind this?
zh: 所以有了这些药物发现模型，想法是：好，我们能不能先创建一个模型，让我们理解制造什么来结合这个才是最好的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's kind of step one.
zh: 那算是第一步。

speaker: Unknown
en: The next step is that, okay, I've made something that can bind here.
zh: 下一步是：好，我制造了能在这里结合的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I also get something that will predict what happens after I bind this thing?
zh: 我能不能也得到能预测我结合这个东西之后会发生什么的模型？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then after that, you also want to be able to predict, okay, but can I also predict what are the unwanted effects that I can get?
zh: 然后在那之后，你还想能够预测：好，但我能不能也预测我会得到哪些不需要的效应？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's kind of the progression of the problems that we're trying to solve with these models.
zh: 那算是我们试图用这些模型解决的问题的演进过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the first step of what molecule binds well is the thing we've actually gotten, you know,
zh: 而且我认为第一步——什么分子结合得好——是我们实际上已经做得

speaker: Unknown
en: Better and better and better at doing.
zh: 越来越越来越好的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But what folks have realized is, OK, now that we're able to do that better, there's still sort of room to grow and room to improve.
zh: 但人们意识到的是：好，既然我们能够把那件事做得更好了，仍然有成长的空间和改进的空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the actual thing that we want to be able to solve next is being able to predict what those effects are.
zh: 但我们接下来真正想要解决的事情，是能够预测那些效应是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And with coding, with math, those things are very verifiable.
zh: 而对于编程、对于数学，这些东西是非常可验证的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I know whether my code compiles or not.
zh: 所以我知道我的代码能不能编译。

speaker: Unknown
en: For these things, I have to also verify, did my molecule work?
zh: 对于这些东西，我还得验证：我的分子起作用了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: So does it bind to the other?
zh: 也就是说，它跟那个结合了吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I can actually test how well does this thing bind.
zh: 我实际上可以测试这个东西结合得有多好。

speaker: Unknown
en: For does this have the effect that I want?
zh: 至于它有没有我想要的效果？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a more complicated question to ask.
zh: 这是个更复杂的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I then have to be able to put it into a cell and see, does this change the cell in the way that I want to?
zh: 所以我必须能够把它放进一个细胞里，看看，这是否以我想要的方式改变了这个细胞？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or to figure out what side effects does this have in a person, I need to first put it into a mouse to figure out, does it do what I want it to do in a mouse?
zh: 或者要弄清楚这对一个人有什么副作用，我得先把它放进一只老鼠体内，弄清楚，它在老鼠身上能做到我想让它做的事吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a saying we always have in research where it's, you know, we've cured cancer in mice 50 times.
zh: 我们在研究中总有一句话，就是，你知道的，我们已经治好了老鼠的癌症 50 次。

speaker: Unknown
en: So everyone's like, look, you know, if you want to cure your cancer, the best thing to do is to be a mouse, right?
zh: 所以大家会说，看，你知道吗，如果你想治好你的癌症，最好的办法就是当一只老鼠，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because we've cured that 50 million times.
zh: 因为我们已经治好过 5000 万次了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have not cured it in all cases in humans.
zh: 我们还没能在所有病例中治愈人类。

speaker: Unknown
en: So oftentimes we'll put it in an animal and say, okay, how does it work in the animal?
zh: 所以我们经常会把它放进动物体内，然后说，好，它在动物身上效果如何？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because that's a good, you know, sometimes that's a proxy for the human, but the real best way to know how's it going to affect you as a person is to put it into another person.
zh: 因为那是一个不错的，你知道的，有时候那是人类的代理指标，但要知道它会对你这个人产生什么影响的真正最佳方法，就是把它放进另一个人体内。

speaker: Unknown
en: So those are kind of the levels of data that we need to figure out.
zh: 所以这些就是我们弄清楚所需的数据的不同层级。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we test it in animals and humans more rapidly?
zh: 我们如何在动物和人类身上更快速地进行测试？

speaker: Unknown
en: Other people are looking at how do we actually get data that will give us good proxies for that?
zh: 其他人在研究我们如何真正获得能为此提供良好代理指标的数据？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's what we actually want the models to be able to predict.
zh: 而这其实才是我们希望模型能够预测的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: But before the models can predict how, well, what effects it'll have, we have to have enough data to train them to make those predictions.
zh: 但在模型能够预测它会产生什么效果之前，我们必须有足够的数据来训练它们做出这些预测。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's a bit of what you're hearing folks say when they say, we need to generate the data to let us do that.
zh: 这就是当你听到人们说「我们需要生成数据来做到这一点」时他们所表达的一部分意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's both data to let us verify the experiments we're doing, but there's now another vertical of, what's the data that will get the models good enough to actually make those predictions?
zh: 既有让我们验证正在做的实验的数据，但现在还有另一个维度，那就是：什么样的数据能让模型足够好，从而真正做出那些预测？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like what would be your crazy goal?
zh: 比如你疯狂的目标会是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And he said for like 88 to 90% success rates.
zh: 然后他说了大概 88% 到 90% 的成功率。

speaker: Unknown
en: For a process right now that has 90 plus percent failure rates, takes 10 to 15 years and costs billions of dollars.
zh: 而对于一个目前失败率高达 90% 以上、需要 10 到 15 年、耗资数十亿美元的过程来说。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what would change for that to happen?
zh: 那么要实现这一点，需要发生什么改变？

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the things I love about ISO, I think there are folks on Twitter who are like, well, you know, ISO, they're really good at sort of, you know, protein folding, but protein folding is not the only problem.
zh: 我喜欢 ISO 的原因之一是，我想 Twitter 上有些人会说，嗯，你知道，ISO 他们真的非常擅长，你知道，蛋白质折叠，但蛋白质折叠并不是唯一的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm like, look, you know, ISO won.
zh: 我想说的是，看，你知道，ISO 赢了。

speaker: Unknown
en: ISO and team invented protein folding with AlphaFold, right?
zh: ISO 和团队用 AlphaFold 发明了蛋白质折叠，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: That is why Demis got the Nobel Prize, was because he created this thing
zh: 这就是 Demis 获得诺贝尔奖的原因，因为他创造了这个东西

speaker: Unknown
en: It's hard to do.
zh: 这很难做到。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's hard to do, which everyone is now kind of enjoying and kind of running at, which is amazing.
zh: 这很难做到，而现在每个人都在某种程度上享受着它、某种程度上在它上面奔跑，这太棒了。
